Subject: Structured output & function-calling follow-up — Crestline Analytics

Hi Susan / Tim,

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps focused on model fit, structured-output evaluation, and the function-calling/retry behavior we discussed. I pulled together an initial prompt set and a lightweight benchmark we can run during the trial.

Recap (quick):
- Primary goal: reliably extract invoice line items + metadata into Crestline's invoice schema with deterministic field types and minimal post-processing.
- Main risks: hallucinated line items, schema drift across vendor invoices, and function-call failures on partial outputs.
- Environment: you prefer GPIO-like on-prem inference later (Private), but will start with a hosted sandbox for qualification.

Recommended models (first-pass):
- redwood/titan-7b-v2-q4f: good latency/cost for smaller batches and tight schemas (recommended for schema-conformance tests).
- redwood/calliope-13b-v1: stronger structured-output consistency on longer contexts (use for recall-focused benchmarks).
- If you need max fidelity for tricky line-item parsing, run a targeted pass with redwood/ascend-33b (non-quantized) for comparison.

Attached: prompt set (crestline_prompt_set_v1.jsonl) and a sample schema (schema_invoice_v2.json). I also attached our quick benchmark CSV with example metrics we usually capture (per-field precision/recall, schema-valid rate, token cost).

Structured-output & function-calling checklist (initial tests):
1) JSON schema compliance: run each prompt through a schema validator and report per-field failure modes.
2) Retry semantics: implement idempotent retries with exponential backoff (start 200ms, *2, max 2s) and a per-request dedupe id — this avoids duplicate downstream processing if the function call succeeds but the response is lost.
3) Partial-output handling: for long invoices, enable prefix/KV cache to preserve context across paginated calls; validate that the runtime returns well-formed partial JSON fragments or returns an explicit truncation marker.
4) Quality regression checks: keep a small set of golden prompts (we included 20 in the prompt set) and run them on each candidate model; fail the rollout if any critical field falls below 95% F1.

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm two data samples for the benchmark (one typical, one adversarial) — Susan suggested dropbox link by EOD Thursday.
- We (Redwood): schedule a 60m sandbox run with a Solutions Engineer to run the structured-output suite (Laura + Vivek).
- After run: short findings note (benchmarks + suggested model/quantization profile), then recommend Dedicated vs Private sizing if you move to on-prem.

If that aligns, I can schedule the run for Thursday 16 May 10:00am PT with Laura and Vivek.

Best,

Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.ai

Susan — quick technical notes ahead of Thursday's run. I'm Laura (SE) and I'll kick off the structured-output suite. A few engineering tips so the sandbox gives you the clearest signal: 

- Model selection: we'll run the shortlist Hannah suggested. For redwood/titan-7b-v2-q4f please expect the tightest latency but slightly higher schema-failure on nested arrays; calliope-13b-v1 tends to produce cleaner nested JSON for multiline descriptions.
- Validation pipeline: we'll run schema validation as a first pass, then field-level fuzzy matching (address/description normalization). We'll output: schema-valid-rate, per-field precision/recall, average tokens, and failure examples.
- Function calling: Redwood supports two modes — structured tool-call (the model returns a structured object that the runtime interprets) and emit+call (model returns JSON which we then map to a function). For Crestline, structured tool-call with explicit argument types will reduce downstream mapping errors.
- Retries & exactly-once: Platform provides idempotency keys and a best-effort de-duplication layer. For true exactly-once guarantees you will need an application-level ack from Crestline after downstream processing; we can surface at-most-once delivery with visibility hooks in the Console. We'll document the recommended pattern in the run notes.

I added two small changes to the benchmark CSV (attached in the Drive link): token-cost-per-invoice and a notes column to flag anonymized PII entries. Also included a short README in the Drive explaining the CSV columns.

See you Thursday — I'll bring a short demo that shows a failing case and how we triage regression.

- Laura
